about: Would You Rather (Live) for CS Quest unit 6 (plan section 7). The dilemmas themselves live in the official game's bank (scripts/data/would-you-rather/en.json, topics tech and online, translated in the 11 other data files); this file adds what the WYR format has no room for: the teacher's prompt after each reveal and the CSTA 2017 ids each dilemma practices. Each item repeats the dilemma's English A/B text (checked against the bank) so the printed prompt sheet can show the two choices next to the prompt: the host and projector screens show the text, never the id, and the eight come in random order. Unscored: the reveal is the class split plus the all-time split. The lesson materialiser links these starters from the Would You Rather (live) step; the prompts print with the lesson.

items.a: A robot that cleans your room
items.b: A robot that cooks your dinner
items.prompt: Who is helped? What would the robot need to sense?

items.a: A phone that never needs charging
items.b: Internet that never drops
items.prompt: Which one changed how people live more?

items.a: A self-driving school bus
items.b: A bus with a driver you know
items.prompt: Who gains, who loses a job, who do you trust?

items.a: Learn from a video you can pause
items.b: Learn from a person you can ask
items.prompt: How has technology changed learning? What did it not change?

items.a: A watch that counts your steps
items.b: A watch that reminds you to drink water
items.prompt: What data does each collect? Who should see it?

items.a: Video-call a relative far away every day
items.b: Visit them once a month
items.prompt: What did people do before video calls?

items.a: A voice helper that knows everything
items.b: One that never listens unless you press a button
items.prompt: What is the tradeoff between handy and private?

items.a: A game that is free but shows ads
items.b: A game you pay for once with no ads
items.prompt: How does the free game make money?

items.a: Live in a town with no internet for a week
items.b: Live in a town with no cars for a week
items.prompt: Which would change your day more? Why?

items.a: A robot teacher for a day
items.b: A robot referee for a game
items.prompt: What can a robot not do well here?

items.a: A map app that picks your route
items.b: A paper map and your own choices
items.prompt: What skill might you lose? What do you gain?

items.a: Translate any language with your phone
items.b: Learn one language really well
items.prompt: How might this change jobs for translators?

items.a: A 3D printer that makes toys
items.b: A 3D printer that makes spare parts for broken things
items.prompt: Which helps more people?

items.a: Headphones that block all noise
items.b: Headphones that let safe sounds through
items.prompt: Who needs to hear the street? Who needs quiet?

items.a: A drone that delivers your lunch
items.b: A friend who brings it on a bike
items.prompt: What job changes? What is nicer?

items.a: A smart fridge that orders food
items.b: A shopping list on paper
items.prompt: What does the fridge know about you?

items.a: Every lesson on a tablet
items.b: Every lesson on paper
items.prompt: What is better on each? Who is left out by each?

items.a: A robot arm that helps a doctor
items.b: A robot that helps a farmer
items.prompt: Which jobs change? Which get safer?

items.a: Computers that write songs
items.b: Computers that only play songs people wrote
items.prompt: Who should get the credit for a computer-made song?

items.a: A job building robots
items.b: A job fixing robots
items.prompt: Which skills from our lessons does each need?

items.a: Everyone online can see your drawing
items.b: Only your family can see it
items.prompt: What could go right? What could go wrong?

items.a: Share one photo with the whole world
items.b: Share ten photos with ten friends
items.prompt: Who else might see them later?

items.a: A nickname online that nobody knows
items.b: Your real first name online
items.prompt: What does a stranger learn from a real name?

items.a: An app that is free if it sees where you are
items.b: An app that costs a little and never knows
items.prompt: What are you paying with?

items.a: Ask a grown-up before every download
items.b: Never download anything
items.prompt: What is the middle path?

items.a: Write your passphrase on paper and hide it at home
items.b: Make one you can remember, nothing written down
items.prompt: Who may know your passphrase? Where is a written one safe?

items.a: Photos only on your tablet, where nobody else sees them
items.b: Also keep a copy on a service someone else runs
items.prompt: What happens when the tablet breaks? Who else can see the copy?

items.a: Use a picture someone else made and credit them
items.b: Draw your own, even if it is worse
items.prompt: What does credit do for the artist?

items.a: A class page where anyone can comment
items.b: One where only your class can
items.prompt: Who might comment? Who moderates?

items.a: Delete an old post you are embarrassed by
items.b: Leave it and laugh
items.prompt: Is anything online ever really gone?

both: What could go wrong with A? With B?

2.wyr-tech: Who is helped, who is hurt, what job changes?
2.wyr-online: What is public, what is private, who else could see it?

scaffold.defend: Defend on every other reveal: one student for A, one for B, thirty seconds each.
scaffold.note: The tech set keeps 20 dilemmas; the lesson hosts 8 at 20 seconds (CA-9). Teachers may host 10 on a block day. The printable prompt sheet shows each dilemma's A/B text beside its prompt (the a/b fields here), because the eight come up in random order and the screens never show an id.
